purpose: Coordination rules for any number of concurrent agents. Rules are keyed by FILE ZONE, never by agent name, so agents can join, leave, or be renamed without rewriting the protocol.
_how_to_adapt: THIS FILE IS THE ONLY SOURCE OF RULES. Everything below describes the MECHANISM, which is universal.
To adopt teamwork-agent in your project: (1) set 'project'; (2) fill 'zones' with YOUR paths;
(3) fill 'verification' with YOUR commands; (4) fill 'contracts_easy_to_break' with YOUR contracts;
(5) fill 'boundaries' with YOUR ports/globs; (6) copy scripts/gates.example.json to scripts/gates.json.
Steps 2-5 are the ONLY project-specific parts. Delete the '_example' zones when you do.
Never rewrite principles, claims, zones_policy, conflict_resolution, done_means or priorities:
that is the part that makes parallel agents stop deadlocking each other.
principles: An agent is never blocked by the absence of another agent. Every rule below is designed so that a missing, renamed, or finished agent cannot stall anyone else.
Ownership is advisory; an active claim is the only thing that actually blocks a file. Zones exist to prevent collisions, not to fence people out.
Coordination files are written only through scripts/agent_handoff.py. Hand edits lose races.
Rules live here and only here. .agent-handoff.json holds live state (claims, task_log, hints), not rules.
A missing zone, gate or contract is not a reason to wait. Fill in what you know; write down the rest as a backlog item.

zones._comment: Zone name -> file patterns. Zone names describe AREAS, not people. Any agent may work in any zone; the pattern only tells you who is likely to be there and what collides.
zones._how_to_adapt: Delete the '_comment' and '_how_to_adapt' keys, replace the 'coordination' zone with YOUR top-level components, and put anything dangerous into 'reserved'. A zone list that no longer matches the repository is worse than no zone list at all: validate will WARN on every nonexistent path and agents stop reading the warnings.
zones._example: The 'reserved' zone is intentionally EMPTY. See reserved_rules.

reserved_rules._comment: The ONLY fenced area. An entry here makes `claim` require an explicit --force. Use it for things whose breakage escapes the repository: OS/network settings, production config, migrations, deploy scripts, secrets. Typically EMPTY in a fresh adoption - an empty list is a valid, safe state.
reserved_rules._how_to_add: Add the path to zones.reserved (a list) and describe it here. Then warn the team via: agent_handoff.py hint "To all: I am taking <path>, reason: ..."

zones_policy.advisory_not_binding: A zone listing never blocks you. It only produces a WARN on claim so you notice someone else works there. Only an active claim on a FILE is a real conflict.
zones_policy.adding_a_zone: If your file matches no zone, claim it anyway. A missing zone is not a reason to wait. Optionally add the pattern to the closest zone.
zones_policy.ownership_by_claim: Who owns a file is decided by the last active claim on it, never by the zone table and never by who appears first in task_log.
zones_policy.names_are_not_zones: Do not add agent names to zones. When an agent leaves, its zone entries would block newcomers forever.

claims.what_blocks: Only an active claim whose files match yours. Everything else is a hint.
claims.one_claim_one_task: A claim is one verifiable task. Do not mix a refactor and a bugfix under one claim, or the gate cannot tell which one it confirmed.
claims.stale_policy: A claim with no heartbeat for stale_after_minutes is treated as ABANDONED. Health-check reports it. You may take those files with --force and say so in coordination_note. Do NOT wait indefinitely for a silent agent.
claims.how_to_take_stale: python scripts\agent_handoff.py claim <you> "<task>" --files <files> --force   # only for stale claims
claims.no_ghost_claims: Always release. If you are interrupted, the stale policy above is the recovery path.
claims.subagents: Take a separate claim named <parent>/<role>. Two workers sharing one name collide silently.
claims.restarted_session: If your name already holds a LIVE claim, you are a restarted session, not a second agent. Take the name <your-name>/2. Silently reusing the name makes the first session's files look free while it still writes them.

conflict_resolution: Re-read the file and .agent-handoff.json; the other agent may have finished.
Keep the newest compatible behavior unless it breaks a tested contract.
Record the conflict and the resolution in your task_log entry.
If the other claim is stale, take the files with --force and say why.

verification.before_claim: Run the gates FIRST so you know the baseline before your change. A red gate you did not cause is not your regression, and you must be able to say which it was.
verification._how_to_adapt: Replace the entries below with YOUR project's commands, or point agents at `python scripts/dev.py gates`, which reads scripts/gates.json. The universal minimum is pytest plus coordination validate; everything else is project-specific and MUST NOT be assumed here.
verification.exit_codes: validate returns 1 only for BLOCKING problems (broken coordination JSON, claim on a missing file, mojibake). Legacy task_log entries are WARN and must not fail the run; a red validate that predates your change is not your regression.
verification.record: Every completed task gets one dated task_log entry via log-entry, with changed_files, verification commands, and measured result.
verification.measured_not_asserted: Record numbers from a real run, not adjectives. 'works' is not a result; '38 passed' is.

done_means: Gates green, checked BEFORE and AFTER your change.
You did not block anyone: if you changed a shared contract, you added a hint.

priorities.P0: gates fail; ImportError/AttributeError/SyntaxError; the main path from input to result is broken; coordination JSON corrupted; a public contract stops being readable
priorities.P1: abandoned task; stale claim; you are blocking another agent; cross-component integration broken by someone else's change
priorities.P2: work inside a zone you claimed
priorities.rule: With an open P0, do not start P3 or P4. Check: python scripts\agent_handoff.py backlog list

contracts_easy_to_break._comment: FILL THIS IN. This is the single highest-value section of the whole template: it is what a new agent reads to know which files it must not casually touch. Leave it empty and every agent re-discovers your breakage rules by breaking them.
contracts_easy_to_break._how_to_add: One key per contract. Name it, say what breaks it, and point at the test that locks it. Example shape: "<contract>": "<what it is>. Changing <what> requires <what action>. Locked by <test path>."
contracts_easy_to_break._example_schema_version: "<module>.<Struct>": "Change the field set only with a new SCHEMA_VERSION; consumers read it by name."
contracts_easy_to_break._example_sentinel: "<numeric field>": "-1 means NOT CHECKED because <budget reason>. Ranking and filtering must treat -1 as unknown, never as clean. Locked by <test path>."

boundaries._comment: FILL THIS IN for your project. Everything here is a place where a well-meaning agent loses work or breaks the machine.
boundaries.test_ports: Use port=0 in tests. Reserve a manual range (e.g. 18900-18999) so two agents cannot fight over a port.
boundaries.caches: Tests use tmp_path; benchmarks use a separate cache file. Never a runtime database as a test cache.
boundaries.temp_trap: Verify where tempfile.gettempdir() points in YOUR environment. In some setups it returns the REPO ROOT, so any mkdtemp() without dir= lands in the working copy. Create scratch dirs explicitly (.scratch/<agent>/<task>/) and delete them in a finally block, including on failure.
boundaries._example_generated: Add your own: artifact directories, model checkpoints, downloaded datasets, anything a run produces.

coordination_files.one_write_tool: scripts/agent_handoff.py is the ONLY way to write .agent-handoff.json, .agent-protocol.json and docs/agent-status.json. This is a single TOOL, not a single AUTHOR: any agent may run it, and nobody is appointed to own a file.
coordination_files.no_lockout: docs/agent-status.json is self-service: every agent writes its OWN agents.<name>.* section via status-set. There is no single-writer owner, because a single-writer rule silently freezes the journal the moment that one agent is absent, which is exactly the deadlock this protocol version removes.
coordination_files.encoding: UTF-8; a BOM may appear, always read as utf-8-sig. Cyrillic saved from cp1251/ANSI becomes mojibake; repair with: python scripts\agent_handoff.py repair-encoding
coordination_files.rules_location: THIS file. .agent-handoff.json -> team_protocol.rules is kept only as a historical pointer and must not be treated as authoritative.
coordination_files.state_location: .agent-handoff.json -> team_protocol.active_claims (live claims), task_log (history), hints (one addressed line each).

workflow: 2. Baseline: run python -m pytest -q (or scripts/dev.py gates) BEFORE changing anything.
3. Check freshness: python scripts\agent_handoff.py status; who-owns <file> for each target.
5. Edit atomically. Re-read a file immediately before writing it if it is not yours.
6. Heartbeat if the task runs longer than 30 minutes.
8. Record: log-entry with changed_files, verification, measured result, coordination_note.
9. Update your section of docs/agent-status.json via status-set.
10. Release the claim and delete your scratch.

dashboard.requires: fastapi + uvicorn (pip install fastapi uvicorn); without them everything else still works
dashboard.mode: read-only; the UI never writes coordination files
dashboard.not_critical: If the dashboard is down or was never installed, work continues normally. It is observation, not infrastructure.

onboarding.note: Paste-ready prompt for any new agent. It contains no agent names on purpose. Adding an agent requires NO protocol edit: pick a name, claim files, work.

normalisation.note: Names that `normalize-legacy` may recognise inside a task_log entry title. Empty means: reuse authors already present in this journal. Do not hardcode names in scripts.

handoff_entry_schema.author: your agent name
handoff_entry_schema.description: what changed and WHY; the reason matters more than the result
handoff_entry_schema.coordination_note: ownership, conflicts, agreements made with other agents
handoff_entry_schema._comment: Keys are the schema `validate` enforces. Missing required fields in a NON-legacy entry is a BLOCKING problem; in a legacy entry it is only a warning. date, author and coordination_note are exempted from the blocking check because old entries legitimately lack them.

backlog.description: EXAMPLE — replace or delete. Fill zones with your real paths, verification with your real commands, contracts_easy_to_break with the contracts a new agent must not break, boundaries with your ports and globs, and copy scripts/gates.example.json to scripts/gates.json.
